title: Human action gates
summary: A recipe step typed operator_gate human_action is the one gate a person finishes: entering their own password or credential, which the agent may not type. Its human_purpose must be password_entry; any other purpose refuses as human_action_misclassified and names the agent-run gate to use instead (machine_browser_approval, admission_owner_approval or admission_invite_entry). The contract refuses keys, ready_text, wait_seconds and any other field, so the step cannot type into the terminal or carry a secret; gate_timeout_seconds bounds the wait at 1..1800. The gate prints one machine_qa.operator_gate line with kind human_action, self_approving false, and instructions naming the step and where to type (the visible Terminal window or its tmux attach command); yoke watch qa-plan emits that line as urgent. It then only reads the terminal: completion_text passes; a denial or expiry fails as human_action_rejected; a setup exit fails as terminal_setup_exited; an expired wait fails as human_action_timed_out; a failed lease renewal fails as human_action_heartbeat_failed; each names a recovery. The step evidence records gate_evidence with the purpose, waited_seconds and self_approving false. Exploratory walkers stop at real password, 2FA or payment steps. They handle consent, the declared Google identity and stray sheets themselves, recording each workaround with evidence and preserving the behavior under test; browser approval cannot be replaced by CLI approval.
